classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: No checks were performed because the required data was not provided. The tool requires a bill of materials (each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency) and a declaration (product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, operations done in the UAE).

procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism through the Factory Registration service. The factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and provide a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for the Certificate of Origin for India e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and submit the application.
Pay the certificate fee online. The fee ranges from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on the invoice value in AED.

Receive the approved certificate, which is issued before, at, or within 5 working days of the date of exportation. The certificate is valid for 12 months from the date of issue and covers only one import. It may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue. India may ask the UAE authority to verify a certificate, and the authority must answer an origin verification request within 90 days, extendable by 60 days.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.

The agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' used in the build-up value-addition method. It also does not state whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

The operations listed in Article 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says. These include simple assembly, labelling, simple packaging, and simple testing.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties still apply. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.
The certificate fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because registration requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The agreement says box 8 for the retrospective issuance mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping, but the CEPA's 5-year requirement governs CEPA claims.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

follow_up_questions: Provide a bill of materials with each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency.
Provide a declaration with the product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, confirmation that final manufacture occurred in the UAE, and description of operations done in the UAE.
Provide the shipment value in AED so that the duty saving and the exact certificate fee can be calculated.
